Article Title: 'Calculated campaign driven by vested political interests': 42 ex-judges back Gyanesh Kumar in open letter
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: A total of 42 former judges on Thursday expressed deep concern over protests targeting Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, saying he had been labelled a "puppet", "thief" and "compromised" in what they described as a "calculated campaign driven by vested political interests".In an open letter, the veterans took strong exception to officers, who conduct the elections, being called names and shamed with "warning of reprisal once power changes hands"."This appears to be a calculated campaign driven by vested political interests, with little regard for the potentially devastating consequences of destabilising the world’s largest democracy," the 42 veterans said."Activist outfits with a long record of selective litigation lend these claims a veneer of legality. They file petition, one after the other. They seldom file proof," the letter said in an apparent attack on CJP, which has been levelling serious charges against CEC Gyanesh Kumar over a reported dissent within the poll body.Veterans also said that "criticism of institutions is a democratic right. Denigration is not".They also hit out at the Congress party , which has doubled down on its verbal assault on Gyanesh Kumar, by questioning how the party's victory through the same EVM goes unquestioned.The ex-service members also highlighted how ECI's demand for sworn declaration was not submitted by the Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi."A party that governed this nation for over five decades now claims that the very system which elected it is rigged. It does not act alone. Activist outfits with a long record of selective litigation lend these claims a veneer of legality. They file petition, one after the other. They seldom file proof," they wrote in a letter.This comes as Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, after hosting a lunch for INDIA bloc leaders for the second consecutive day, declared that the opposition would be heading to Gandhi Memorial for a peaceful sit-in.Whereas, Rahul Gandhi again attacked Gyanesh Kumar, along with PM Modi, home minister Amit Shah and RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat, accusing them of "hijacking democracy" through criminal conspiracy.The party on Thursday said the opposition was fighting to protect democracy, voters, and the common people of the country.The development comes amid the opposition's ongoing protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Kharge hosted the lunch for INDIA bloc leaders at a restaurant in the national capital on Thursday.Meanwhile, CJP founder Abhijit Dipke accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of "murdering democracy and vote theft," and said protests will go on till CEC Gyanesh Kumar resigns from his post.Presiding over a protest held by civil society group and CJP here against SIR, he alleged that voter deletions under the Special Intensive Revision were aimed at disenfranchising those opposed to the BJP and accused PM Modi and the Election Commission of murdering democracy and causing vote theft.
Article Summary: 42 former judges express concern over protests targeting Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. They say he has been labelled a "puppet", "thief" and "compromised" in what they described as a "calculated campaign driven by vested political interests"

Article Title: 39,815 rural families get pucca houses in Uttarakhand under PMAY-G
Article Text:
Chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami

DEHRADUN: As many as 39,815 rural families in Uttarakhand have been provided pucca houses under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Gramin (PMAY-G) since 2022, with Udham Singh Nagar recording the highest number of houses constructed, according to state government figures.Udham Singh Nagar accounted for 4,882 houses, followed by Haridwar with 4,493 and Rudraprayag with 4,032. Chamoli recorded 3,900 houses, while Pithoragarh and Pauri accounted for 3,386 and 3,195 houses respectively. Uttarkashi saw 3,057 houses constructed under the scheme.Chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami has been seeking additional housing allocations from the Centre under both the rural and urban components of the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana . The state government said Uttarakhand has also received national-level recognition for its performance under PMAY-Urban 2.0.Launched in 2016, PMAY-G aims to provide pucca houses with basic amenities to homeless families and those living in kutcha or dilapidated houses in rural areas. Under the scheme, eligible beneficiaries receive financial assistance of Rs 1.30 lakh per house through direct benefit transfer into their bank accounts.The state has also increased assistance for purchasing kitchen utensils and other kitchen-related items from Rs 5,000 to Rs 6,000 from 2022-23 onwards.Beneficiaries are provided an additional Rs 12,000 for toilet construction under the Swachh Bharat Mission through MGNREGA/SWajal.Under the BB Ramji Yojana, beneficiaries are also provided 95 days of wage employment for construction of their houses. The housing support is supplemented with access to basic services such as drinking water, LPG connections under the Ujjwala scheme and electricity connections.“Under the guidance of Prime Minister Narendra Modi ji, our government is committed to providing a pucca house to every needy family. We are continuously working to ensure that the benefits of PMAY-G reach every eligible family,” Dhami said.Other districts covered under the scheme include Dehradun with 2,839 houses, Champawat with 2,789, Bageshwar with 2,279, Tehri with 2,134, Nainital with 1,480 and Almora with 1,349 houses.
Article Summary: As many as 39,815 rural families in Uttarakhand have been provided pucca houses under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Gramin. Udham Singh Nagar recorded the highest number of houses constructed, according to state government figures.

Article Title: 'Criminal conspiracy to hijack India': Rahul ups the ante against govt, CEC
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi at protest site

Rahul Gandhi: 'Around 300 MPs' want to protest

Kharge leads MPs towards Gandhi Memorial

Why is the INDIA bloc protesting?

What happened during Wednesday's protest?

Three FIRs filed over Wednesday protest

What triggered the row over SIR?

NEW DELHI: The INDIA bloc's confrontation with the Election Commission escalated on Thursday as Opposition leaders regrouped in Delhi for a third consecutive day, with Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi saying around 300 MPs from both Houses wanted to stage a peaceful protest but had been stopped for two days.Rahul Gandhi, who was detained during Wednesday's protest, said the Opposition would continue its campaign against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and alleged that the government and the Election Commission had "hijacked India" and "stolen votes". He said the Opposition would ensure that those it holds responsible are brought to justice.Congress president and Rajya Sabha leader of opposition Mallikarjun Kharge, meanwhile, said INDIA bloc MPs were heading to the Gandhi Memorial for a peaceful sit-in and prayer. The latest mobilisation came after opposition MPs were stopped from proceeding towards Jantar Mantar on Wednesday, several leaders were detained and Delhi Police registered multiple FIRs over the protest.Speaking in Delhi on Thursday, Rahul Gandhi said MPs from both the Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha had been prevented from holding a peaceful protest for two consecutive days."Around 300 MPs—from the Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha—wish to stage a peaceful protest. We have been prevented from protesting for two days now. On the first day, we were stopped outside the Election Commission. Subsequently, we expressed our desire to protest at Jantar Mantar, yet yesterday, as you witnessed, we were stopped there as well; our people were assaulted.The reality is that Narendra Modi, Amit Shah, Gyanesh Kumar, and Mohan Bhagwat have hijacked India through a criminal conspiracy, destroyed the Constitution, and stolen votes. We, the Opposition, assure you that action will be taken. They will be brought to justice. This is our guarantee. You will see these four individuals brought to justice"Rahul Gandhi was speaking as he attended the second lunch meeting of opposition MPs at Connaught Place along with Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy and other INDIA alliance MPs.The meeting was hosted by Kharge and came a day after the Opposition's attempt to march towards Jantar Mantar ended with police stopping the protesters and detaining several leaders, including Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra Mallikarjun Kharge said the INDIA alliance would proceed to the Gandhi Memorial for a peaceful sit-in after the lunch meeting."We, the members of the INDIA alliance, are heading to the Gandhi Memorial to stage a peaceful sit-in protest. We will sit there and pray that the BJP government, specifically PM Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah be granted the wisdom to realize that their actions are not in the nation's interest. Whether it is the issue of vote theft, the rising inflation, the problems facing the youth, or any other crisis they have created, everything goes against the public interest. That is why we are going to the Gandhi Memorial to pray; we want to highlight that they are snatching away the freedom we secured, the freedom won for us by great leaders like Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, Mahatma Gandhi, and Vallabhbhai Patel and are making every effort to destroy it. They are taking away our right to vote. We are going there to pray that they be granted the wisdom to stop stripping us of our rights and freedoms—including the right to vote—that were secured for us by these great leaders. We will sit there and stage a protest"The fresh protest plan marks another attempt by the Opposition to maintain pressure on the Election Commission after its march towards Jantar Mantar was stopped on Wednesday.The Opposition has been demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.Congress leaders have repeatedly said that the INDIA bloc will continue its campaign until Kumar resigns, while the BJP has rejected the Opposition's allegations and questioned its criticism of an Election Commission that conducted elections in states where Opposition parties came to power.The issue has also been framed by Congress leaders as a wider concern over the electoral process rather than merely a demand for the removal of the CEC.Congress MP Kodikunnil Suresh said earlier on Thursday that the Opposition had no intention of backing down."And today also, we have a strong protest, an aggressive protest against Gyanesh Kumar. We are not going back," Suresh said.He said the INDIA bloc leadership would decide its next strategy and that subsequent protests would be led by Rahul Gandhi, Kharge, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other Opposition leaders."Our ultimatum is for Gyanesh Kumar to resign from the Chief Election Commissioner post. If he is not ready to resign the post, the government should remove him from Chief Election Commissioner," Suresh said.The latest mobilisation follows a tense day in Delhi on Wednesday when INDIA bloc MPs attempted to proceed towards Jantar Mantar to protest against Gyanesh Kumar and the SIR process.Delhi Police stopped the march, after which Opposition leaders staged a sit-in. Rahul Gandhi was among those detained and was taken to Barakhamba Road Police Station. He was seen attempting to open a barricaded gate as police prevented protesters from moving ahead.Priyanka Gandhi Vadra was also detained and taken to Chhatrasal Stadium. During the police action, she was seen lying on the ground and later alleged that force had been used against the protesting MPs."What is the value of the Constitution in this nation? We will lay down our lives for the Constitution. No cost is too high for us," Priyanka Gandhi told reporters while waving a copy of the Constitution from the police vehicle.Rahul Gandhi subsequently said the Congress and INDIA bloc would continue taking to the streets, even if it meant arrests and legal cases."To save the Constitution and democracy, the Congress Party and the opposition are ready to take to the streets as many times as needed, face arrests, or endure legal cases."This alliance between the dictatorial Modi government and the Election Commission has already been exposed. It is time for resignations and action. An arrogant regime cannot hold out for long against the fervour of the people."He also said the Opposition would continue protesting until Gyanesh Kumar resigns."We are not going to stop protesting till Gyanesh Kumar resigns. This is a fight to protect the most sacred thing in this country. There is nothing that Narendra Modi and Amit Shah can do that will stop us," he said.Delhi Police has registered three FIRs in connection with Wednesday's Opposition protest, with more cases being registered, according to the police.The cases relate to allegations including assault on police personnel, obstruction of government work, pushing and manhandling, and misbehaviour with police personnel.The names of Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra also figure in the details of the FIRs registered so far.The latest cases add to an earlier FIR related to the Opposition's protest outside the Election Commission.On Tuesday, INDIA bloc MPs had planned a march from Parliament House towards Nirvachan Sadan, the Election Commission headquarters. Police said no official permission had been sought or granted for the proposed march.After protesters were stopped near the Election Commission office, several Opposition leaders staged a sit-in. Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra later entered the Akashvani Bhavan premises along with other leaders and continued their protest there.Police said the protesters were asked to leave but allegedly refused, insisting that a delegation of MPs be allowed to meet Election Commission officials. Police subsequently intervened, removed the protesters from the premises and detained them.The police account of Wednesday's confrontation also emerged on Thursday.Delhi Police constable Ankit Kasana alleged that he was assaulted by demonstrators during the detention of Rahul Gandhi near Jantar Mantar.Kasana, who is posted at Parliament Street police station, said he was deployed for crowd control when security personnel attempted to move Rahul Gandhi after his detention."Yesterday around 6:30, when we were at our duty points, there was a detention going on there. We suddenly found out that Rahul sir had been detained. As soon as we had to get his car out safely because these people weren't letting us through there sometimes they would lie down in front of the car, sometimes they would stop the car and push it. As we were trying to turn the car, a private vehicle blocked the way. We saw that there were some Congress supporters," Kasana told ANI.He alleged that around 30 to 35 people, including men and women, surrounded him while Rahul Gandhi was being detained. He alleged that the group abused him, tore his uniform, scratched him and bit him."Some leaders tried to hijack that car, forcefully trying to snatch the keys. At the same time, I reached there and moved those people away. During this, an Inspector took the car into his custody and started backing it up so we could safely move Rahul Gandhi from there. As soon as they saw that I was alone and sir was inside, someone grabbed my collar from behind, tore my uniform, and broke my button too."Kasana was subsequently taken to Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital for a medical check-up."We actually help the public a lot, and that's why the public trusts the Delhi Police. But if these people want to destroy that trust, we won't let that happen. No matter how much they harass us or abuse us, we won't be aggressive. We'll do our duty peacefully. We have to maintain law and order, and we'll make sure we do," he said.Congress leaders have linked the campaign against Gyanesh Kumar to wider allegations concerning the electoral rolls and the SIR exercise.Congress MP Manickam Tagore accused the BJP and the government of protecting the CEC and questioned why the Opposition was being prevented from protesting."This is the Gujarat model which they (central govt) wanted to expand across India. what we are asking now. What was the LoP Rahul Gandhi asking for from the first day?... We were stopped at Akashwani Bhavan. Rahul Gandhi sat under that tree. Therefore, there is an FIR on it. Now yesterday we went to Sagar Ratna restaurant. From there we went, we wanted to go to Jantar Mantar. The police stopped us. Then now there is again an FIR against Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi. What HM Amit Shah and PM Modi are doing, we are unable to understand. They are clueless at first. They are not able to understand what is the issue we are speaking about. We are asking for the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation... why are they giving him this much protection?... They are afraid of that mobilization across India. Rahul Gandhi has emerged as the leader on those issues which have been affecting this country. It is not only about the CEC. It is about the electoral process they completely hijacked," he said.Congress MP Imran Masood also raised allegations concerning deletion of voters from electoral rolls."Until this loot stops and the 13 crore people whose voting rights were cut are restored, this fight will continue. What is the meaning of democracy if such a huge number of voters are removed? The number of names cut in the name of Bangladeshis is more than the population of Bangladesh itself... What is the meaning of the Election Commission..."The Election Commission has maintained that differing views and observations are part of institutional deliberations and that its orders carry legal sanction and follow established statutory procedures.The INDIA bloc's campaign also spread beyond Delhi on Thursday, with RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav joining a protest in Patna against Gyanesh Kumar.Yadav alleged that Opposition MLAs had been stopped by police."Our MLAs have been stopped by the police. They are not letting us move," Yadav said.He accused PM Modi, Gyanesh Kumar and Amit Shah of vote theft and said the protesters were marching towards Raj Bhavan."We are holding a march to the Raj Bhavan today. We are marching because of the way Gyanesh Kumar, PM Modi, and HM Amit Shah have orchestrated vote theft and worked to destroy the country's democracy. We are marching today to demand punishment for the conspirators who plotted to destroy our democracy," he alleged.The Patna demonstration centred on the Opposition's allegations of irregularities in the SIR process and its demand for the removal of the CEC.The BJP has rejected the Opposition's allegations and attacked Rahul Gandhi over the protests.BJP national president Nitin Nabin described Rahul Gandhi and his supporters as having an "anarchist mindset" and accused them of trying to spread "poison" in society.“I can only say that they are of 'arajaktawadi' (anarchist) mindset and trying to spread poison in society. If he had such objections, elections in Kerala were also conducted by the same Election Commission. The election in Tamil Nadu, where they have come to power, was also conducted by the same Election Commission,” Nabin said.“If Rahul Gandhi has the courage, he should first resign. The people are watching the manner in which he is playing this game,” he said.Nabin also accused the Leader of Opposition of protecting infiltrators and said the BJP would oppose attempts to settle people in India with what he described as a "foreign mindset".The Congress has been demanding Gyanesh Kumar's resignation amid allegations concerning decisions and orders related largely to the SIR process.The Indian Express had reported that election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had objected on record at least 14 times over the previous 10 months to decisions and orders, mostly concerning the SIR exercise.The Election Commission has maintained that differing views and observations are part of deliberations in any institution. It has also said its orders have full legal sanction and follow established statutory procedures.The Opposition has continued to demand greater transparency and accountability from the poll panel, making Gyanesh Kumar's resignation its central demand.
Article Summary: Opposition leaders regroup in Delhi for a third consecutive day. Rahul Gandhi says around 300 MPs from both Houses wanted to stage a peaceful protest. Opposition MPs were stopped from proceeding towards Jantar Mantar on Wednesday. Delhi Police registered multiple FIRs over the protest.

India and Kazakhstan reviewed the entire spectrum of their bilateral relations and reaffirmed their commitment to working more closely to translate their strong partnership into tangible outcomes.The conversations happened at a meeting between Kazakhstan's recently appointed deputy foreign minister Arman Issagaliyev and India's Ambassador to Kazakhstan, YK Sailas Thangal, according to the ANI report."Amb YK Sailas Thangal had a warm and productive meeting with the newly appointed Deputy Foreign Minister of Kazakhstan. The two sides reviewed the entire gamut of bilateral relations and reaffirmed their commitment to working even more closely to translate the strong India-Kazakhstan partnership into tangible outcomes," the Indian Embassy in Kazakhstan said in a post on X."They discussed ways to seize emerging opportunities, deepen mutual understanding, and further strengthen a forward-looking partnership between India and Kazakhstan," added.The meeting came weeks after Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev held talks on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi and reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening the strategic partnership between the two countries.According to the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), Modi highlighted India's deep historical and civilisational ties with Kazakhstan and expressed satisfaction over the steady growth of bilateral relations in recent years.“The two leaders reviewed bilateral cooperation in a range of fields, including political, trade, defence and security, connectivity, energy, critical minerals, emerging technologies, creative economy, and people-to-people ties.They also exchanged perspectives on regional and international developments,” the MEA said.“The leaders reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthen the strategic partnership between the two countries, for the mutual benefit of their people, as well as for peace, stability, development and prosperity in the region,” it added.Tokayev visited New Delhi to attend the 18th BRICS Summit, held on September 12 and 13. During his visit, he also attended a gala dinner hosted by Modi for the visiting dignitaries at Bharat Mandapam on September 12.
Article Summary: The conversations happened at a meeting between Kazakhstan's recently appointed deputy foreign minister Arman Issagaliyev and India's Ambassador to Kazakhstan, YK Sailas Thangal. The meeting came weeks after Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev held talks on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit.

Article Title: Times Prime rolls out Rs 1 lakh reward envelopes across 5,000 Daalchini vending machines
Article Text:
Times Prime takes 'Born to Reward' to Daalchini vending machines

Times Prime has partnered with Daalchini as part of its ‘Born to Reward’ birthday campaign, placing 1,00,000 limited-edition reward envelopes across 5,000 Daalchini vending machines in Mumbai and Delhi.The campaign, which runs from September 23 to October 31, offers consumers reward envelopes priced at Rs 10, each containing a voucher with benefits worth over Rs 5,000 from participating Times Prime partners.Five of the envelopes contain Golden Tickets, with each ticket offering a reward package worth up to Rs 20,000. The package includes enhanced benefits from participating Times Prime partners as well as access to an exclusive Times Prime event.Consumers can locate participating Daalchini vending machines through timesoffer.daalchini.co.in.The vending machine activation is part of Times Prime’s broader birthday campaign, which began on its app. From September 23 to 30, members unlocked a new partner offer each day, with the offers remaining available for redemption for the rest of the campaign.The offers cover categories including travel, shopping, wellness, beauty, healthcare and lifestyle, with participating brands including Flipkart Flights, Klook, IGP, MeraDoc, FirstCry, Geetanjali Salon, GIVA and Duolingo.Prerna Kalra, co-founder and CEO of Daalchini, said the partnership reflects the growing role of vending machines in providing consumers with instant access to products and offers.“India’s instant commerce story has been about delivery in minutes. We believe the next chapter is zero-wait, with value available the moment you walk past a machine. Gift cards and vouchers are a big step in that direction, and Times Prime’s birthday is the perfect moment to put rewards into consumers’ hands, literally,” Kalra said.Times Prime is a digital lifestyle membership platform from Times Internet that offers subscriptions, benefits and experiences across entertainment, dining, travel, shopping, wellness and other lifestyle categories.
Article Summary: Times Prime has partnered with Daalchini as part of its ‘Born to Reward’ birthday campaign. The campaign, which runs from September 23 to October 31, offers consumers reward envelopes priced at Rs 10. Article Title: 'I have not come here for regime change': Dhruv Rathee during CJP protest in Bengaluru

NEW DELHI: YouTuber Dhruv Rathee on Thursday said, “I have not come here for regime change”, while participating in a protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, demanding his immediate resignation over alleged irregularities in the SIR, news agency PTI reported.Rathee joined CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and actor-activist Prakash Raj at Freedom Park, where they took part in a protest organised under the banner of ‘Janata Nyayalaya’ against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The protesters demanded the immediate resignation of Kumar over alleged irregularities in the SIR exercise.Addressing the gathering in Bengaluru, Rathee said, “I have not come here for regime change.” He also alleged that there was “zero transparency and zero accountability from the EC” over the SIR exercise.Dipke said protesters would continue their agitation until Kumar stepped down. “We will hit streets, reclaim democracy, continue agitation till CEC resigns,” Dipke said.Actor Prakash Raj further demanded that the SIR exercise be scrapped, alleging that it was not merely about deletion of votes but also concerned the dignity and rights of citizens.He also alleged that CEC Gyanesh Kumar was “acting at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah”.A large number of women, students and other members of civil society gathered at Freedom Park, with protesters raising slogans demanding that the SIR exercise be scrapped and Kumar resign.According to organisers, the protest was organised as a “people's tribunal” for people affected by the SIR exercise across Karnataka. They said it would be followed by a “Chappal protest” in solidarity with women.Posters at the protest carried slogans including “Error 404 - Name Not Found”, “It's done bro, resign sir” and “Don't erase us, hear us”.Police said tight security arrangements had been put in place at the venue to prevent any untoward incident.
Article Summary: YouTuber Dhruv Rathee took part in a protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar. Protesters demanded his immediate resignation over alleged irregularities in the SIR exercise. Rathee alleged that there was “zero transparency and zero accountability from the EC’

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Thursday condemned recent attacks on two airports in Saudi Arabia's Riyadh by Yemen's Iran-linked Houthi group, calling the targeting of civilian infrastructure “completely unacceptable”.MEA issued a statement saying that the attacks on Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh had resulted in civilian deaths and injuries.“India condemns the attacks over the past few days targeting Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, which have resulted in civilian deaths and injuries,” the MEA said.READ ALSO: Malaysia bets on AI boom with 2,300-acre Silicon Island “The targeting of civilian infrastructure is completely unacceptable. We express our deepest condolences to the families of those who have lost their loved ones. We wish speedy recovery for those injured. We express solidarity and stand with the people and government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia,” it added.Three people were killed and 36 injured in attacks on the two Saudi airports over two days, according to Saudi authorities cited by the BBC.Two people were killed and 28 wounded in an attack on Abha International Airport, the General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) said on Wednesday.In a separate attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, one person was killed and eight others were injured, it said. The attacks took place on October 6 and 7, although GACA did not specify which airport was targeted on each day.Two women, who were Moroccan and Algerian nationals, were among those killed in the Abha attack, according to GACA.The attacks, for which the Houthis have claimed responsibility, mark an escalation in the renewed fighting between Saudi-backed government forces and the Iran-aligned Houthi group in Yemen.Saudi Arabia’s civil aviation authority did not identify those responsible for the attacks. However, Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group had targeted both Saudi airports with ballistic missiles and drones.Saree also claimed that the Houthis attacked Aden International Airport in Yemen on Wednesday. The airport is a major international gateway for areas of Yemen outside Houthi control and has been targeted during previous bouts of fighting.He said the attacks on the Saudi airports were carried out in “response to the Saudi aggression against our country”, which he claimed involved “60 airstrikes and missile attacks in the past 24 hours”.Earlier in the day, the Houthi group also issued a “last warning” to global airlines operating flights through Saudi airspace, saying the area had become a “theater for our military operations”.The group also claimed it had attacked King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh with a ballistic missile. There was no immediate confirmation from Saudi Arabia of the latest claim.Saree said the missile “struck its target with precision and caused the disruption of airport operations.”“We reiterate our call and warning "for the last time" to all global airlines regarding the consequences of continuing to operate flights in Saudi airspace, which has become a theater for our military operations,” Saree said.He added that airspace over the “sacred areas” in Mecca and Medina was exempt from the warning. The Houthi warning came amid heightened concerns over attacks on Saudi airports and airspace.The US Mission in Saudi Arabia on Wednesday urged American citizens to exercise heightened vigilance amid Houthi threats. It warned that the situation could lead to flight cancellations, airspace closures and other travel disruptions.
Article Summary: India condemns recent attacks on two airports in Saudi Arabia's Riyadh by Yemen's Iran-linked Houthi group. Three people were killed and 36 injured in attacks on the two Saudi airports over two days, according to Saudi authorities. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group had targeted both Saudi airports with ballistic missiles and drones.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday condoled veteran actor Nana Patekar , remembering his “immense” contribution to Hindi and Marathi cinema and praising his versatility and creativity.In a post on X, PM Modi wrote: “Few actors possessed the intensity, individuality and unmistakable presence that Shri Nana Patekar Ji had. He brought remarkable versatility and creativity to every role and gave us characters that will be remembered for generations. He was also admired for his frank and forthright views, never hesitating to express what he believed in.”He added: “Shri Nana Patekar’s contribution to Hindi and Marathi cinema was immense. His passing leaves a deep void. My condolences to his family, friends and countless admirers. Om Shanti.”While speaking at an event in Delhi, PM Modi remembered veteran actor.“This morning we got the news that the renowned actor Nana Patekar is no longer with us. He was an exceptional artist who won the hearts of audiences through a variety of roles,” PM Modi said.The Prime Minister said Patekar’s life was dedicated to the “honour and glory of the Tricolour” and used references to some of the actor’s well-known films to describe his career.“Nana Patekar’s life was dedicated to the honour and glory of the Tricolour. He refused to be bound by constraints; like a ‘Parinda’, he soared through the vast skies of cinema,” PM Modi said.He said Patekar used his films to raise questions about social issues and challenge the prevailing order.“Through his films, he launched scathing attacks on the prevailing societal order. He was a true Krantiveer who fought against social evils,” PM Modi said.PM also recalled Patekar’s distinctive screen presence, saying, “His silence was as impactful as his speech was powerful.”The Prime Minister said Patekar consistently spoke against anti-national elements and paid tribute to the actor while offering condolences to his family and admirers.“I pay tribute to Nana Patekar and offer my condolences to his family and admirers,” PM Modi said.Meanwhile, Union home minister Amit Shah also mourned Patekar, sharing a picture with the veteran actor and calling his passing an “irreparable loss” to the world of art.In a post, Shah wrote: “Over five decades, with his natural acting and powerful dialogue delivery, he left an indelible mark on the hearts of audiences. Whether it was serious social issues or humor-satire, he brought to life every character he portrayed. Through the 'Naam Foundation,' serving drought-stricken farmer families, or going to the border to boost the morale of soldiers, even after reaching the pinnacle of fame, he remained connected to his roots. ”He added: “Whenever I met him, his simplicity and straightforwardness always left a deep impression. May God grant strength to the grieving family and fans to bear this sorrow, and may the departed soul find a place at His divine feet.”Defence minister Rajnath Singh also paid tribute to Patekar, writing: “Nana Patekar was not merely an actor; he was an institution in himself. His remarkable contribution to Indian cinema will continue to inspire generations.”Patekar suffered a cardiac arrest at his home in Goa and was found unconscious. He was rushed to a hospital, where doctors declared him dead.Known for films including Prahaar, Parinda, Krantiveer, Tirangaa and Welcome, Patekar was one of the most recognised actors in Hindi and Marathi cinema.
Article Summary: PM Modi pays tribute to veteran actor, hails ‘immense’ contribution to cinema. Patekar suffered a cardiac arrest at his home in Goa and was found unconscious. He was rushed to a hospital, where doctors declared him dead.

Article Title: Stock market crash today: BSE Sensex tanks over 1,000 points; Nifty50 at 22,231 - top reasons for fall
Article Text:
Adding to the pressure on markets, Brent crude prices rose another 2%.

Why is stock market down today?

RBI’s policy stance change

US bond yields

soar to 24-year high

Oil jumps above $102/barrel

FIIs continue to sell

Fed rate hike worries

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

Stock market crash today: BSE Sensex and Nifty50 , the Indian equity benchmarks, crashed in trade on Thursday, with both indices down over 1%. Investors reacted to the RBI’s policy tightening and repo rate hike, continued FII selling and other negative factors. BSE Sensex plunged over 1,000 points while NSE Nifty50 slipped to 22,231 levels.At closing, Nifty50 was at 22,231.80, down 371.25 points or 1.64%. BSE Sensex was at 71,593.24, down 1,045.46 points or 1.44%. The sharp decline erased over Rs 11 lakh crore from the combined market capitalisation of companies listed on the BSE.ITC, Adani Ports, IndiGo, Power Grid and Reliance Industries (RIL) were among the biggest losers on the Sensex, with their shares declining as much as 4%. On the other hand, Titan and major IT stocks such as Tech Mahindra, HCL Technologies, TCS and Infosys gained up to 2%, providing some support to the benchmark index.The RBI delivered its first rate increase in nearly four years. However, market analysts viewed the central bank’s decision to move its policy stance from ‘neutral’ to ‘calibrated tightening’, against a difficult global geopolitical backdrop, as the more significant signal for markets.Jefferies expects the RBI to raise interest rates by around 100 basis points during the current tightening cycle.Nomura also pointed to the change in stance as an unexpected development. “We believe this was aimed at anchoring inflation expectations and building a buffer against adverse global conditions. However, the message was mixed, with the MPC clarifying that “calibrated tightening” only signalled “no rate cuts”, and indicated data dependence going forward,” it added.VK Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments Limited says that the calibrated tightening stance of the RBI has implications for markets.“With two more rate hikes of 25bp each likely in this rate hiking cycle, there will be pressure on valuations rising from higher fixed income returns. Investor preferences also might shift marginally towards interest inelastic segments like pharmaceuticals,” he says.The global selloff in bonds intensified, sending yields to their highest levels in several years. The US 30-year bond yield climbed above 5.71%, while the yield on benchmark 10-year notes rose past 5.3%. The two-year note yield also moved close to 4.9%.Rising bond yields generally make debt markets more appealing to investors, which can increase pressure on emerging-market equities. Since bond prices and yields move in opposite directions, a sharp rise in yields indicates significant selling in the bond market.Adding to the pressure on markets, Brent crude prices rose another 2% to move above $102 per barrel. Investors remained worried about the security of Middle East oil supplies as attacks on shipments increased in the Gulf and around the strategically important Strait of Hormuz.Tankers travelling through the Strait of Hormuz faced the highest number of attacks in a single week since the Iran war began earlier this year, even as Gulf producers raised exports. The increase in attacks came as crude shipments from the Gulf increased, but with greater risks and higher costs for cargoes and crews. On Wednesday, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency said a tanker north of Qatar had been hit by multiple projectiles, resulting in casualties.Meanwhile, US crude inventories fell by 3.2 million barrels last week to 424.1 million barrels, according to the Energy Information Administration on Wednesday. A Reuters poll of analysts had forecast a smaller decline of 1.7 million barrels.The record selling spree of FIIs continues, exacerbated by the rising bond yields. Foreign investors continued their selling spree in Indian equities on Wednesday, offloading shares worth more than Rs 6,121 crore on a net basis, according to provisional NSE data. Their net selling has now reached nearly Rs 57,000 crore across nine straight sessions through Wednesday.Since the start of September, FIIs have been net sellers in 20 of the 25 trading sessions. Their sustained selling, despite brief periods of buying, has continued to weigh on Dalal Street since the Middle East war began earlier this year.VK Vijayakumar notes that a distinct and strong trend in the market in recent months has been the increasing preference for growth stocks over value stocks.“Growth stocks are being accumulated at high valuations while value stocks are languishing at fair valuations. Sustained selling in large-caps by the FIIs have contributed significantly to this trend. With the US 10-year bond yield hovering above 5.3%, FIIs will continue to sell on every rally. This will put the Nifty large-caps under pressure for some more time,” he warns.“A reversal in this trend will happen only when FIIs turn buyers, and there is no clarity on when this will happen. In brief, this frustrating period in the market might continue for some more time. Remaining invested in value stocks will be rewarded in the long run. Investors should also look at the good opportunities in fixed income in this rising rate environment,” he adds.Minutes from the Federal Reserve's meeting showed a split among policymakers last month over the case for raising interest rates. Some officials believed a hike was needed to contain the effects of energy and other price shocks, while a more hawkish group saw higher rates as necessary to guard against emerging inflation driven by demand.Traders currently see only an 18% probability of a rate increase later this month, while the odds of a December hike are being priced at 80%, according to CME's FedWatch tool, as cited by Reuters.
Article Summary: BSE Sensex plunged over 1,000 points while NSE Nifty50 slipped to 22,231 levels. Investors reacted to the RBI’s policy tightening and repo rate hike, continued FII selling and other negative factors. The sharp decline erased over Rs 11 lakh crore from the combined market capitalisation of companies listed on the BSE.

NEW DELHI: The Delhi Police is examining several mobile phone videos to identify protesters allegedly involved in the assault and obstruction of police personnel during a Congress protest near Jantar Article Title: From 'vote chori' to 'chita andolan': Street protests return with a new playbook
Article Text:
Street protests are back, this time with new tools

During the INDIA bloc’s protest against the CEC, Priyanka Gandhi lay down on the road, daring anyone to move her.

The street has always been a political stage

How social media changed street mobilisation

Beyond Jantar Mantar: The protests away from the spotlight

Protest on women's sa​fety in Delhi

Protesters stage the 'Chita Andolan' in Madhya Pradesh's Panna district, demanding compensation and rehabilitation.

The street is old, the tools are changing

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Slogans are ringing out, crowds are turning up and the streets are once again abuzz with protests.On Tuesday, INDIA bloc MPs took their protest against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls to the national capital, demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. The march took an unexpected turn when Rahul Gandhi surprised the police with a last-minute change of course, turning it into a sit-in.A day later, opposition MPs were back with another dramatic flash protest on Janpath streets, where Priyanka Gandhi Vadra lay down on the road and refused to budge until the CEC agreed to meet opposition leaders.And more could be coming. Cockroach Janata Party’s Abhijeet Dipke, who rallied young protesters during the anti-NEET paper leak agitation in July, has warned of a “Jantar Mantar 2.0” on October 10 if the CEC does not resign.But Delhi is not the only place, and politicians are not the only ones taking their grievances to the streets. Across the country, protests over very different issues are bringing people out in an attempt to make their voices heard.The protests differ in scale, issue and leadership. But together, they point to something familiar returning to the foreground: street politics.Peaceful protests have always been a part of our democracy.India's politics has rarely been confined to Parliament, party offices or election rallies. The streets have always had a part to play.Mahatma Gandhi turned marches, boycotts and satyagraha into instruments of mass politics during the freedom struggle. Decades later, Jayaprakash Narayan's movement drew students and citizens onto the streets against the Indira Gandhi government.Anna Hazare's anti-corruption protests filled Jantar Mantar and Ramlila Maidan in 2011. The anti-CAA protests saw prolonged sit-ins, while farmers camped at Delhi's borders for more than a year before the three farm laws were repealed.Street politics, then, is hardly new. What keeps changing are the tools used to trigger, spread and sustain mobilisation. Political analyst Uday Chandra feels social media is making protests more visible while also changing who can start and sustain them."Social media certainly makes protests visible to millions, enabling a rapid or viral spread. But it also does something more important: it reduces dependence on political parties, unions and established organisations to mobilise people. A grievance may now turn into a movement before conventional political actors decide how to respond," Uday Chandra says.But the current round of protests goes beyond social-media amplification, feels Chandra."I think something real is happening beyond social-media amplification. Street protest never quite disappeared from politics in India, but for much of the past decade, electoral politics under a highly centralised party machinery overshadowed it. What we are seeing now is, to my mind, the re-emergence of the street as an autonomous political arena," he said.What stands out in this round of protests is not just the issues being raised, but who is often raising them first.On questions ranging from examinations to electoral rolls, young people have managed to create pressure outside the usual party machinery. Increasingly, political parties have found themselves responding aggressively to issues they did not start.So, have young people and students shown political parties the way back to street mobilisation? The events surrounding the NEET protests in July this year are a case in point.As students protested over the paper leak, Jantar Mantar became the centre of an agitation that continued for weeks. The CJP emerged as the pressure group leading the agitation and eventually ensuring the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Union education minister.Many political parties that initially stood on the sidelines scrambled to join the agitation. On July 21, Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Mallikarjun Kharge and other opposition leaders staged a sit-in outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence over police action against students protesting the NEET paper leak.But Chandra argues that the CJP, as a movement, differs significantly from political parties and earlier large movements such as the Anna Hazare agitation or the farmers' protests."CJP is much more decentralised than the two movements you mention. The Anna movement had recognisable leaders and a national campaign/agenda. Likewise, the farmers’ protests rested on strong unions, local organisation, and the economic capacity to sustain mobilisation for months. By contrast, what we see emerging now is networked, relatively leader-light, and often issue-specific," he said.The CJP advantage is also organisational, he feels."Instagram, WhatsApp, YouTube and other online platforms can connect previously unrelated groups rapidly. Mobilisation is, therefore, not only faster but more fluid. You do not necessarily need to build and register an organisation before launching a movement. Increasingly, the movement precedes the organisation," Chandra adds.It is perhaps this realisation that has forced political parties to course-correct their mobilisation strategies.Rahul Gandhi, who faced criticism for prioritising his "Chhatron ki Goonj" campaign instead of backing the anti-NEET protests led by CJP, has now made a more direct attempt to help Congress enter the protest space. On October 4, he launched the 'Satyagraha' portal, which seeks to map protests across the country and connect people agitating over different issues.For Chandra, the move shows that Congress has recognised the risks of ignoring protests that begin online and then spill onto the streets."The Satyagraha platform strikes me as an attempt to situate the INC within an emerging ecology of anti-BJP protests. This is an interesting shift in political organisation. It takes the party from a traditional top-heavy high command structure to a node connecting diverse and dispersed struggles against the status quo."The high-decibel protests against Gyanesh Kumar or over NEET are only one part of the story, perhaps the more visible one. Away from the national spotlight, peaceful protests have been taking place across the country over a wide range of issues.They may be small, localised and often unconnected: women’s safety, land, displacement, water, facilities in schools, local governance and more. But together, they show how the street remains an important space for people trying to make themselves heard.In Delhi, young women have marched over women's safety after cases of sexual violence. Demonstrations have also spread to cities including Mumbai, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Ahmedabad, Patna and Dehradun, with protesters demanding safer public spaces and greater accountability from governments and police.In Madhya Pradesh’s Panna district, families affected by the Ken-Betwa river-linking project have revived their "Chita Andolan". Protesters have slept on funeral pyres, stood in water and gone on hunger strike over compensation and rehabilitation.In Maharashtra’s Maval, farmers opposing the Pavana closed pipeline project announced a 'jal samadhi' agitation while also demanding rehabilitation for families that surrendered land for the Pavana dam decades ago.Water has also brought farmers onto the streets in Karnataka, where organisations in Krishna basin districts have opposed releasing reservoir water to Telangana, arguing that drought-hit areas within Karnataka should be given priority.At IIT Bombay too, students have turned their protest over the death by suicide of student Sahil Wakode into a hunger strike, with the JNU Students’ Union joining calls for action on the demands raised by protesters.The scale and demands vary sharply. Some protests involve thousands; others are confined to a university campus, a few villages or even a handful of streets. They may target the Centre, state governments, local administrations or institutions, but the impulse is the same: take the grievance to the street.So, street politics is old, but the mobilisation techniques have changed. Earlier movements depended heavily on student organisations, unions, public meetings and, later, television coverage. Today, a protest can begin on Instagram or X before it reaches Jantar Mantar.Social media has also changed the language of protest. A slogan shouted on the street can become a meme within hours, while posters, one-liners, chants and songs travel far beyond the protest site.Recent demonstrations have offered plenty of examples. At women's protests in Delhi, slogans such as 'Ek kachori, do samosa, in mardon ka kya bharosa' quickly travelled from the street to Instagram reels, using humour and rhyme to make a serious point about women's safety and gender attitudes.At the Mumbai protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, placards carried lines such as 'Gyanu must go' and the Bollywood-inspired 'Vote churaya mera, kisne o sanam? Gyanu ne'. Days later, Rahul Gandhi carried the Gen Z-style message "Gyanesh, it's done bro!" during the INDIA bloc's march to the Election Commission. Whether it will culiminate into effective but what it definitely did was make people stop and notice.And Gen Z may not be the youngest generation learning to protest.In Lucknow, around 200 schoolgirls blocked a road in the rain over a shortage of teachers and a damaged road leading to their school. In Fatehpur, around 1,000 students staged a four-hour protest demanding drinking water and repairs to classrooms. In several cases, authorities acted after the protests.What has changed is not the instinct to protest, but how quickly a grievance can find an audience and become visible. The slogan may now become a meme and the mobilisation may begin on a phone screen. The destination, however, is often still the same: the street.
Article Summary: Street protests are back, this time with new tools. Priyanka Gandhi lay down on the road, daring anyone to move her. The street has always been a political stage. But the tools used to trigger, spread and sustain mobilisation are changing.

NEW DELHI: India used the UN stage to turn Pakistan’s own words against it, arguing that the terror networks Islamabad once nurtured have now come back to haunt their own backyard, a reality, New Delhi said, that even Pakistan’s leaders have begun to acknowledge. India also urged the international community to take stronger action against states accused of sponsoring terrorism.Speaking at the UN General Assembly’s Sixth Committee, which deals with legal affairs, India’s first secretary Raghoo Puri said Pakistan had long portrayed itself as both a victim and a frontline state in the fight against terrorism."Pakistan has presented itself as a frontline state in combating terrorism and as a victim, while masking the fact that the Frankenstein’s (monster) the Pakistani state has created and lost control over have moved from wreaking havoc in neighbouring countries to doing the same in Pakistan," Puri said on Wednesday."This was exposed recently by a provincial chief minister of Pakistan, and may I jog the memory of colleagues to an interview in 2018 by her father and former prime minister of Pakistan, exposing this dark secret," he said."You cannot run with the hares and hunt with the hounds," Puri warned. "Reality never works like that".Puri was responding to remarks by Pakistan’s deputy Permanent Representative Usman Jadoon, who had launched an attack on India during the committee proceedings.Puri pointed to recent remarks by Punjab chief minister Maryam Nawaz , who said her province faced a bigger threat from neighbouring Pakistani provinces than from neighbouring countries.Maryam Nawaz, who leads Pakistan’s Punjab province, said last month in Lahore: "Unfortunately, the threat Punjab, a province of 130 million, faces comes less from my neighbouring countries and more from my neighbouring provinces."Earlier this month, she also questioned the idea of distinguishing between different forms of extremist violence, saying anyone involved in terrorism should be treated as a terrorist regardless of their political motives.Puri also referred to an interview given by Maryam Nawaz’s father, former Pakistan prime minister Nawaz Sharif, to Dawn in 2018. Sharif had spoken about militant groups operating from Pakistan and questioned whether they should be allowed to cross the border and carry out attacks in India."Militant organisations are active. Call them non-state actors; should we allow them to cross the border and kill 150 people in Mumbai?" he had said.Puri did not name either Maryam Nawaz or Nawaz Sharif while making his remarks.Puri also hit back at Pakistan’s claims about the outcome of Operation Sindoor , India’s counterterror military action to the Pahalgam attack."If bombed-out airfields and cratered runways look like victory to Pakistan, they are, of course, welcome to enjoy it," he said.He accused Pakistan of continuing to spread false claims about the operation and said its approach was part of a wider campaign of disinformation.Puri said the "Pakistani representative’s desperation to falsely tout the Pakistani military’s narrative on the outcome of Operation Sindoor" was consistent with Pakistan’s long-running use of state-backed misinformation and psychological warfare.Puri also took a swipe at Pakistan after its delegation made a second intervention, repeating what he described as old arguments."Pakistan believes in the circular economy of words and narratives," Puri said."If this much effort had actually been made in countering terrorism rather than narrative building, misinformation, and disinformation, the world would have been a better place," he said."But nothing more can be expected from a Form 47 government," he added, referring to Pakistan’s political system and alleged manipulation of the electoral process.Puri also challenged Pakistan’s claims on minority rights and accused Islamabad of allowing religious extremism to flourish."The victims in Pahalgam were not asked about their political orientation; they were asked about their religion," Puri said."It is therefore deeply ironic that Pakistan speaks of combating religious hatred while allowing the conditions that enable it to persist and thrive, especially by fomenting cross-border terrorism," he added.Puri referred to the Pahalgam terror attack, in which terrorists targeted tourists after asking about their religion.He said the attack showed the consequences of allowing extremist groups and crossborder terrorism to continue.Puri also questioned Pakistan’s claims that it was taking action against Jaish-e-Mohammed chief Masood Azhar, who is listed by the UN as a terrorist.Pakistan had increased the reward for information leading to Azhar’s arrest from Pakistani rupees 50 lakh to 70 lakh."Pakistan glosses over its state support for terrorism by announcing enhanced rewards for apprehending UN-listed head of Jaish-e-Mohammed, terrorist and mastermind of several attacks against my country," Puri said."When the media can reach Masood Azhar and get confirmation from him about the success of Operation Sindoor, surely the Pakistani state knows his whereabouts," he said.Azhar had earlier appeared in a video in which he claimed that his family infrastructure had been destroyed during India’s strikes on Bahawalpur as part of Operation Sindoor.Puri also recalled Pakistan’s earlier claims that Jaish-e-Mohammed was no longer active."Just a few months ago, Pakistani representatives used this forum to call the Jaish-e-Mohammed a defunct organisation," Puri said. "The world has seen the script play earlier, and we are clear-eyed that this time also it is going to be no different."Puri warned that allowing terrorist groups to operate with political protection could undermine international efforts against terrorism."When terrorist groups are allowed to operate under state political power, international commitments become meaningless, and when perpetrators are provided safe havens, the victims of terrorism are denied justice," he said.He also cited the example of al-Qaeda leader Osama bin Laden, who was found in Abbottabad, Pakistan, years after the 9/11 attacks."The world has not forgotten 9/11, and where its perpetrators, including Osama bin Laden, were caught," Puri said.He then pointed to the 2008 Mumbai attacks."The world has not forgotten 26/11," when Pakistani terrorists killed 166 people in Mumbai, he said. "The world has not forgotten Pahalgam."Puri also referred to Pakistan’s record on terror financing and the upcoming meeting of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF)."The world is aware of Pakistan’s financial support to terrorism, as also, the FATF plenary meeting coming up soon," he said.The FATF, the global body that monitors terror financing and money laundering, is scheduled to hold its next plenary meeting in Paris from October 26 to 30.
Article Summary: Pakistan has long portrayed itself as both a victim and a frontline state in the fight against terrorism, India's first secretary Raghoo Puri said. Puri was responding to remarks by Pakistan’s deputy Permanent Representative Usman Jadoon, who had launched an attack on India during the committee proceedings.

Article Title: Beyond condoms: WHO blueprint for new male contraceptives
Article Text:
Contraceptive choices for men. (Reuters)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Men could have more contraceptive choices beyond condoms and vasectomy, with the World Health Organization (WHO) releasing its first global blueprint for developing novel male contraceptives, including daily pills or gels, longer-acting injections and implants, sperm-function blockers and reversible methods that block sperm transport.The WHO's Target Product Profiles (TPPs) do not approve or launch any new contraceptive. Instead, they set minimum and optimal standards for the effectiveness, safety, reversibility, acceptability and affordability of future male contraceptives. The framework covers three approaches: suppressing sperm production, inhibiting sperm function and blocking sperm transmission or transport.The move comes as research into male contraception gathers pace, with several candidates already in clinical trials. RISUG (reversible inhibition of sperm under guidance), developed in India, has completed Phase 1 and Phase 2 studies, while another hydrogel-based method, ADAM, is in Phase 1 trials.Hormonal candidates including nestorone/testosterone gel, dimethandrolone undecanoate (DMAU) and 11β-methyl-19-nortestosterone dodecylcarbonate (11β-MNTDC) are also being investigated.For methods that suppress sperm production, WHO's minimum target is for 90% of men to achieve sperm concentrations of 1 million or fewer sperm per millilitre within 12 weeks, with a 12-month cumulative pregnancy rate of no more than 7%.The optimal target is 95% achieving this level within eight weeks, with the pregnancy rate at 3% or less.The proposed methods include daily tablets or gels, injections every three, six or 12 months and implants lasting at least a year. WHO's optimal profile also calls for sperm concentrations to return to the normal reference range within six months of stopping treatment.Another strategy is to leave sperm present but disable functions needed for fertilisation, such as motility and capacitation. A third is to block sperm transport through the vas deferens, potentially using reversible hydrogels, or temporarily block ejaculation with medication.WHO said the field is rapidly progressing, with several candidates in advanced clinical trials. The new profiles are intended to provide developers and regulators with a common framework for bringing future male contraceptives through research and development.
Article Summary: The WHO's Target Product Profiles do not approve or launch any new contraceptive. Instead, they set minimum and optimal standards for the effectiveness, safety, reversibility, acceptability and affordability of future male contraceptives. The framework covers three approaches: suppressing sperm production, inhibiting sperm function and blocking sperm transmission or transport.

Article Title: WHO puts stroke, cancer, mental health on 10-year traditional medicine research agenda
Article Text:
The World Health Organization has set forth a comprehensive research agenda for the upcoming decade, focusing on pivotal health conditions such as stroke, mental health, cancer, and reproductive health.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: From stroke and cancer to mental health and pain management, the World Health Organization has identified major health conditions for research into traditional, complementary and integrative medicine over the next decade.Its 2025-2034 research agenda identifies stroke, mental health, pain management, musculoskeletal conditions, cancer, metabolic and endocrine disorders, and reproductive health and childbirth as priority areas. Prevention and health promotion, healthy ageing and healthy childhood are also included.The report highlights a striking mismatch between disease burden and research. Stroke ranks third globally in causes of mortality and disability, yet less than 1% of traditional, complementary and integrative medicine-funded grants address the condition. Mental health ranks eighth among contributors to disability-adjusted life years, but the review found very few or no grants specifically focused on mental health conditions. Musculoskeletal conditions are also a prominent cause of disability globally but remain under-researched relative to their burden.Cancer, too, features among the priority areas, with the report noting rising global incidence and calling for research into integrative oncology and palliative care.For metabolic health and endocrine disorders, WHO identifies the need for stronger evidence, including longer-term studies on conditions such as type 2 diabetes and metabolic syndrome.WHO says the aim is to generate stronger evidence on effectiveness, safety, regulation and health-system integration so countries can make informed decisions about the role of these approaches in healthcareThe research agenda also puts patient safety under the spotlight. It calls for studies on herb-drug interactions, monitoring and reporting of adverse events, regulatory and quality-assurance systems, and the safe integration of traditional, complementary and integrative medicine into primary healthcare.The push comes against a broader funding gap. WHO says traditional, complementary and integrative medicine is widely used globally, with use reaching up to 80% of populations in some settings, while less than 1% of global health research funding is directed towards research in the field.India has a direct connection to the agenda. The WHO report acknowledges financial support from the Ministry of Ayush, Government of India, for its development and publication. India was also among the health ministries that participated in the Second WHO Global Summit on Traditional Medicine, held in New Delhi in December 2025.The report, however, is a research-prioritisation framework rather than a clinical guideline or recommendation to use any particular traditional medicine.
Article Summary: The 2025-2034 research agenda identifies stroke, mental health, pain management, musculoskeletal conditions, cancer, metabolic and endocrine disorders. Prevention and health promotion, healthy ageing and healthy childhood are also included. Stroke ranks third globally in causes of mortality and disability, yet less than 1% of traditional, complementary and integrative medicine-funded grants address the condition.

An Indian Council of Medical Research-National Institute of Nutrition (ICMR-NIN) study involving 203 adolescents found that the visual appeal of food images was significantly associated with their willingness to consume the food.Researchers showed adolescents attractive “foodporn” images of healthy foods on Instagram for 15 days and compared them with regular images. The strongest differences were seen for millet porridge and boiled chana salad, whose attractive images generated about 50% and 10% more positive responses, respectively, than their regular counterparts. The difference was statistically significant for the millet and pulse categories.The study used 15 food images divided into three categories: unhealthy foods presented as “foodporn”, healthy foods presented in an attractive “foodporn” format, and healthy foods shown as regular pictures. The researchers also conducted in-depth interviews with 19 adolescents to understand what made food images appealing.Researchers found that the intervention showed a broader positive trend, with adolescents reporting more favourable attitudes towards healthy foods, greater consumption and stronger intentions to eat them, although not all changes were statistically significant.Intentions to consume millet porridge and chana salad were 9% and 15% higher, respectively, for attractive images than regular ones, but neither difference was statistically significant.Visual appeal appeared important, with adolescents citing colour, presentation, ingredients, angle, texture, glossiness, balance and symmetry as factors that made food images more appealing. Even before the intervention, 60% said they were willing to try foods seen on social media, while 56% said attractive food images made them crave them.Adding nutritional information did not significantly alter responses, suggesting that adolescents paid more attention to the visual presentation than accompanying text.The findings suggest that making healthy foods visually appealing could help counter the dominance of attractive unhealthy-food content online, with potential applications in school canteens, restaurants and cafes. However, the study did not establish that attractive food images change actual eating behaviour. The intervention was short, relied partly on self-reported responses, and could not establish causality.
Article Summary: Researchers showed adolescents attractive “foodporn’ images of healthy foods on Instagram for 15 days and compared them with regular images. The strongest differences were seen for millet porridge and boiled chana salad, whose attractive images generated about 50% and 10% more positive responses, respectively.

He was responding to a question on whether the rupee market was irrational."Markets can be quite irrational in the short run. It's only in the long run that they are able to find the right value," he said.The governor said RBI would support the rupee's orderly movement and help it find its "correct value", while ensuring there was no excessive volatility.Malhotra also said a correction in the valuation of global AI stocks could redirect foreign capital to emerging markets such as India. He said a correction in AI stocks would not have a major negative impact on India and "if at all, there may be" a positive impact.Malhotra said that US tariffs and the absence of a trade deal would be a negative but could be offset by a trade deal with other countries.Despite a robust services trade surplus and strong net remittance receipts, the current account deficit widened in July because of a higher merchandise trade deficit, Malhotra said.The merchandise trade deficit rose to $58.7 billion in July and Aug from $55.1 billion in the same period a year earlier, mainly because of higher imports of electronic goods and crude oil. On external financing, Malhotra said net FDI had shown sustained improvement, with inflows rising to $13.8 billion in the first four months of the year from $9.6 billion in the corresponding period a year earlier. The increase was driven by higher gross inflows and a slowdown in the growth of outward FDI."Robust gross FDI reflects the strong interest of global investors in India," he said. FPI recorded net outflows of $10.3 billion during the period up to Oct 5. However, capital-flow measures announced in the June policy had supported inflows, he said. The balance of payments is consequently expected to record a healthy surplus this year.Malhotra also clarified that the new trade rules are aimed at improving ease of business and do not impose a reporting burden on individuals who get paid from overseas for software or other services. NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Wednesday agreed to examine a plea seeking recall of its recent split verdict on whether challenges to the 2023 law governing the appointment of the chief election commissioner and election commissioners should be referred to a larger Constitution bench.On Sept 23, a bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma gave split opinions on whether a batch of pleas challenging the validity of a 2023 law that excludes the CJI from the selection panel should go to a Constitution bench.Justice Datta declined the Centre's request for such a reference, while Justice Sharma favoured placing the matter before a larger bench.It had said due to a difference of opinion, the matter would be placed before CJI Surya Kant on the administrative side for the constitution of a bench of appropriate strength for an effective and authoritative adjudication.On Wednesday, a bench comprising the CJI and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was told about the recall application by senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan. "We will examine and take a call," the CJI said.Sankaranarayanan told the bench that the recall application had earlier been mentioned before a bench headed by Justice Datta, but the matter had been released and he was asked to mention it before the CJI.When the CJI asked whether there was any other interlocutory application, Sankaranarayanan said a curative petition had also been filed. "That, I think, will have to go in its own form," he said.The petitions had challenged the constitutional validity of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, which replaced the selection mechanism laid down by SC in its March 2, 2023 judgement.In that ruling, a five-judge Constitution bench had directed that the CEC and ECs be appointed by the President on the advice of a committee comprising the PM, the leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha and the CJI. Parliament subsequently enacted the 2023 law, under which the selection committee comprises the PM, a Un-ion Cabinet minister nominated by the PM and the leader of the opposition in LS.
Article Summary: Supreme Court agrees to examine a plea seeking recall of its recent split verdict. Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma gave split opinions on whether a batch of pleas challenging the validity of a 2023 law that excludes the CJI should go to a Constitution bench.

Article Title: Doctors, hospitals can't use AI to create testimonials: National Medical Commission
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Doctors and hospitals cannot use AI to create patient testimonials, clinical outcomes or promotional content, nor can they pay to manipulate rankings like those on search engines and apps, under new ethical advertising guidelines issued by National Medical Commission Tuesday, effective immediately.NMC has barred registered medical practitioners and hospitals from using AI-generated content to advertise their services, solicit patients or disseminate unverifiable information about diagnoses, treatments or outcomes. AI cannot be used to create synthetic patient testimonials, voices, clinical outcomes or fake endorsements, or misrepresent the nature or quality of medical services.Doctors can't pay for manipulate search rankings. They also can't make unverified claims such as "best", "number one", "most trusted", "guaranteed cures" or "100% success".Doctors cannot engage influencers, advertising agencies or online platforms in arrangements involving payment linked to procuring patients. Doctors and hospitals cannot offer limited-period discounts, coupons, gift packages or referral benefits if these are likely to encourage unnecessary consultations. However, NMC allows doctors to use social media for factual, non-promotional health education. Hospitals can similarly share objective details.The guidelines restrict the use of patient photographs without valid consent and safeguards. Patient testimonials, before-and-after images and treatment-success claims that could create unrealistic expectations or mislead are also prohibited.NMC has prescribed a warning and mandatory ethics training for a first violation, censure and monetary penalty for a second, suspension for three to six months for a third, and six to 12 months for serious violations. Repeated violations can lead to removal from the medical register for one to three years.
Article Summary: New ethical advertising guidelines issued by National Medical Commission Tuesday. Doctors and hospitals cannot use AI to create patient testimonials, clinical outcomes or promotional content. They also can't pay to manipulate rankings like those on search engines and apps. But doctors can use social media for factual, non-promotional health education.

Article Title: Stark 73% decline in the average size of monitored wildlife populations since 1970, India presents ground for hope: WWF Living Planet Report
